answer: Pay graders by peer prediction, not plain agreement. Each grader submits a score plus a forecast of how the rest of the panel will score, and a Bayesian Truth Serum rule rewards reports that prove more common than forecast. Before scoring, graders whose score-and-forecast vectors match across many epochs are merged into one voice, so an operator hiding a reef of clone graders in one harbor can't inflate the frequency it bets on; each extra head just splits one payout. Independent judgment stays the ferrous core.
